nodes.name: PBSC Synthesis
nodes.procedure: PrBa0.5Sr0.5Co2O5+δ (PBSC) was synthesized as a tetragonal perovskite phase (space group: P4/mmm) matching reported XRD data.
nodes.source_text: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the as-obtained PBSC and PBSCF matched well with the reported data (Figure 1a)

nodes.name: PBSCF Synthesis
nodes.procedure: PrBa0.5Sr0.5Co1.6Fe0.4O5+δ (PBSCF) was synthesized as a cubic perovskite structure (space group: Pm-3m) matching reported XRD data.
nodes.source_text: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the as-obtained PBSC and PBSCF matched well with the reported data (Figure 1a)

nodes.characterization_summary: PBSC shows tetragonal perovskite phase (space group P4/mmm), PBSCF shows cubic perovskite structure (space group Pm-3m).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of the as-obtained PBSC and PBSCF matched well with the reported data (Figure 1a), suggesting the successful formation of the perovskite phases as targeted.

nodes.characterization_summary: No obvious morphological distinction between PBSC and PBSCF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: and there was no obvious morphological distinction between PBSC and PBSCF either based on images recorded by a scanning electron microscope (SEM) (Figure S3a-d, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine PBSC and PBSCF highly crystallized with lattice fringes matching XRD results; PBSC-CV possesses ≈2-4 nm thick amorphous layer while bulk remains crystallized; PBSC+Fe_exo^3+ inherits amorphous layer-coated structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Images recorded by a high-resolution transmission electron microscope (HR-TEM) indicated that the pristine PBSC and PBSCF were highly crystallized (Figure S4a,b, Supporting Information), where the lattice fringes (planes) agreed well with the XRD results.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous elemental distribution of Pr, Ba, Sr, Co in PBSC; even Fe distribution in PBSCF confirms successful B-site doping; external Fe^3+ successfully introduced and evenly distributed in PBSC+Fe_exo^3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping images of PBSC (Figure S4c, Supporting Information) indicated the homogenous distribution of Pr, Ba, Sr, and Co, while the evenly distributed Fe in PBSCF (Figure S4d, Supporting Information) further supported the successful B-site Fe-doping in the lattice.

nodes.characterization_summary: Dynamically balanced surface Fe content around 10-12 at%; O 1s shows increased oxidative oxygen species (O2^2-/O^-) from 11.2% (PBSC) to 36.0% (PBSC+Fe_exo^3+); reduced lattice oxygen indicating increased oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the dynamically balanced surface atomic content of Fe was around 10-12%, as determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS).

nodes.characterization_summary: PBSC-CV shows hydr(oxy)oxide species (CoOOH); PBSC+Fe_exo^3+ shows Co-O-Fe at 685 cm^-1 plus FeOOH and CoOOH phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra of PBSC-CV (Figure 5d) and PBSC+Fe_exo^3+ (Figure 5e) exhibited additional characteristic peaks. The majority of extra peaks in Figure 5d could be ascribed to hydr(oxy)oxide species (e.g., CoOOH).

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show EPR signal at g=2.003 from oxygen vacancies; PBSC+Fe_exo^3+ has highest signal intensity indicating highest oxygen vacancy concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PBSC, PBSCF, PBSC-CV, and PBSC+Fe_exo^3+ had representative EPR signals at g = 2.003, which were recognized as unpaired electrons trapped by the oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: A-site cation leaching confirmed: ([Pr]+[Ba]+[Sr])/[Co] ≈0.94 for PBSC-CV and ([Pr]+[Ba]+[Sr])/([Co]+[Fe]) ≈0.89 for PBSC+Fe_exo^3+; ([Ba]+[Sr])/[Pr] ≈0.85 for both.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the atomic ratios of ([Pr] + [Ba] + [Sr]) / [Co] of PBSC-CV and ([Pr] + [Ba] + [Sr]) / ([Co] + [Fe]) of PBSC+Fe_exo^3+ were determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to be ≈0.94 and ≈0.89

nodes.characterization_summary: Specific surface areas of PBSC and PBSCF are comparable.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface areas of PBSC and PBSCF were comparable (Figure S2, Supporting Information).
